A long time ago, I was part of a mathematics mailing list that ended because of one single person, that spend all day sending lots of huge emails with gibberish arguing that pi is rational. Several people tried to point mistakes, but he would not listen, or, if he listened, he would raise the same point again latter on. It was so much stuff that every other (actual math) discussion stopped and the list died.

Did anyone ever mention that pi is not calculated as 22/7 (which I'm guessing is where he got pi is rational from), 22/7 is just an estimation, the actual calculation is 4/1-4/3+4/5-4/7+4/9-4/11 ad infinitum? Therefore how could it be rational, if the means of calculating it isn't?

People had all kinds of arguments, but it was talking to a brick wall. He wasn't even using the 22/7 approximation, it was a whole other weird ratio that he arrived at through numerology. His argument boiled down to, pick these two numbers a and b, that I arrived at because reasons+mysticism, now draw a circle with length a and diameter b. See, pi is rational! You are all stupid!

That was also a "Cantor's Diagonal Argument is wrong" guy, but this came on waves, usually only once every month.

Just something I realised now and I think there is a misunderstanding: just because there is a series that converge to pi, it does not mean that pi is rational or not. Pi is not defined by a series (it is defined by the roots of trigonometric functions, themselves defined via power series), but there are several series that converge to it, the rationality/irrationality has a priori nothing to do with it.

Just look at the usual misunderstanding that some people have about 0.9999... and 1: when you writes 0.9999... what one means is the series 9/10+9/100+9/1000+9/10000+.... This series converges and it is equal to 1.
Except that series does NOT equal one, it approaches a limit of one, there is significant difference.
